content_html_sanitized:
Canadian Justice Minister, Martin Cauchon has announced that the government will decriminalize cannabis possession early next year.
See
 Walters Concedes That Canada Can Legalize Cannabis If It Wants To, Which Was The Only True Thing He Said While In Montreal.

Only the timing is a surprise. Prohibitionists claim that the announcement was made now to distract the public from the Canadian government's seemingly endless scandals, and perhaps to take the focus off the proposals for safe-injection sites for hard drugs. They may be telling the truth, for once.

Under the Canadian parliamentary system the law will be whatever the Prime Minister wants it to be, so only the details are in question, and, as always, the devil is in the details.

The new law will probably apply to an ounce or less, and possibly some cultivation for personal use. Possession will still carry a fine, and if it is in the C$300 to C$500 range as some reports indicate, it will be just one more instance of decriminalization for the rich and prohibition for the peasants. Let them eat Prozac.

As I said in July, the danger is that the police will increase enforcement to milk the cannabis community for fines. This would be a step backward in Vancouver.
See
 Canadian Justice Minister Cites UK Move In Trial Balloon on " Decriminalization. " Police Want to Keep " Hammer. "

Moreover, being allowed to grow an ounce is not really very meaningful, and the bulk of the supply will remain in the black market with hard drugs. The real danger is that the government will seek to appease the police by increasing penalties for cultivation, which would be a great gift to the narks allies in organized crime.

Over the last several years, I have been almost alone in reporting the amazing degree to which Canadian narks are willing sacrifice Canadian sovereignty to DEAland's agenda.
See
 The Agenda for the Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and links

In September, I reported that the head of the Canadian Police Association told the Washington Post that Canadian had surpassed Mexico, as the a supplier of cannabis.
See
 The Prohibitionist Police State Versus The People. Analysis By Richard Cowan

Again, I have been almost alone in reporting that seizures at the Canadian border are less than one percent those at the Mexican border.

The DEA's own web site says, Virtually all the marijuana smuggled into the United States, whether grown in Mexico or shipped through Mexico from lesser sources such as Central America, is smuggled across the U.S./Mexico Border.

Nonetheless, this morning DEAland Drug Czar John Walters was on Canadian television claiming that the RCMP told him that 95% of BC's $5 billion dollar cannabis crop is exported to DEAland. He said something similar on his recent visit to Vancouver.

Of course, the Czar's own web sitesays, The ONDCP study What America's Users Spend on Illegal Drugs reports that in 2000 Americans spent an estimated $10.4 billion on marijuana. The same report also estimates that Americans consumed 1,009 metric tons of marijuana in 2000.

In order for Walters claim to be correct, the DEAland cannabis market would have to be at least $200 billion, or at least twenty times the government's own estimate of $10 billion!

Of course, the Czar's web site says, Canada is becoming a source country for indoor-grown, high-potency (15 to 25 percent THC) marijuana destined for the United States. Such indoor-grow operations have become an enormous and lucrative illicit industry, producing a potent form of marijuana that has come to be known as " BC Bud. "

The U.S. Customs Service (USCS) reported that marijuana seizures along the British Columbia- Washington State land border, which totaled 325 pounds in 1994, increased to nearly 2,900 pounds in 1999.

Wow! Except that there are seizures bigger than that almost daily at the Mexican border. On December 5th the Laredo Express Newsreported, the Customs Service reported Tuesday it confiscated 6,428 pounds of marijuana in a single seizure at Laredo's World Trade Bridge.

In other words, at one Mexican border crossing in one day's time, twice as much cannabis was seized as was seized at the BC border in a year.

And if Americans consumed 1000 metric tons, and seizures at the BC border were just over one metric ton, then BC Bud seizures represented only one thousandth of the DEAland market.

As for BC bud having 15 to 25 percent THC well don't pack for Canada because of that. BC Bud is no different from indoor weed grown anywhere else. Also, this is another example of trying to pass off an extreme as an average.
See
 The Drug Czar Harvests BC Bud Propaganda Campaign At Canadian Border. The Jails Are Full, But He Likes That.

The RCMP's Drug Situation in Canada - 1999 report said, The average THC content of all samples analysed since 1995 is about 6%.
See
 RCMP Annual Report On the " Drug Situation in Canada " Contradicts Staples Of the Prohibitionist Party Line. Exclusive To MarijuanaNews.

The Dutch government reports that the average THC content of Dutch-grown cannabis has not risen in recent years and now measures 8.6%, with an exceptional measurement of 25% in a single case (Trimbos Institute, 2000).

Is it credible that BC growers, using essentially the same genetics as the Dutch, have somehow greatly surpassed them in indoor growing techniques?

But the RCMP and the Canadian Police Association are collaborating with the DEA to create the impression that the proposed change in Canada's cannabis law is a threat to a Drug-Free America. The threat is purely political. Canadians need to wake up to the fact that their police are lying to them to maintain DEAland style prohibition.
See
 Canadians Need to Examine The Role of the Police In Maintaining Marijuana Prohibition. Paying For Lies That Distort Public Policies and Undermine Sovereignty. Analysis by Richard Cowan
